introduction: These readings speak of what prayer does. Some are statements: that the law of prayer belongs to every religion, that a single verse said with joy outweighs much reading, that work done in the spirit of service is worship and that words without action advance nothing, that prayer heals at a distance and brings tranquillity. Most are prayers themselves, or assurances from Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that they are praying for the person addressed and that the prayer is heard. A hundred of the guide's three hundred quotations are read here, ten from each tenth of the reading order, beside a hundred from elsewhere. Most stand alongside: the Psalms, the Lord's Prayer and the Fatiha, Jesus on the closet and on two or three gathered, James on the prayer of faith, the Qur'an's 'I am nigh', Nehemiah praying and setting a watch, Herbert and Coleridge and Tagore on work and love as prayer. Ten push back or add a side: Paine and Emerson against asking for things, 'your Father knoweth what ye need before ye ask', the psalm that cries and is not heard, Paul's unremoved affliction, Gethsemane, Marcus Aurelius turning the prayer round, Bacon on counting only the answers, Job's scoffers, and Confucius, whose praying 'has been for a long time'.
questions: What do the readings say prayer accomplishes: in the one who prays, in the one prayed for, in the world?
'Without action nothing can be accomplished', and 'work done in the spirit of service is worship'. How do prayer and work stand to each other here, and in Nehemiah and Aesop?
Paine thought petition an attempt to change God's mind; Jesus said the Father knows our needs already. What then is asking for?
Paul's affliction stayed; a psalm cries and hears nothing. How do the readings prepare someone for a prayer that seems unanswered?
Much of this guide is one person telling another, 'I am praying for you'. What does that do?
Bacon warns that we count the hits and forget the misses. How can a person be honest about answered prayer?

outside.why: A psalmist says: evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and he shall hear my voice.
The penitent's psalm asks: create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
Jesus warned against vain repetitions, by those who think they shall be heard for their much speaking.
In the parable a tax collector, standing afar off, says only 'God be merciful to me a sinner', and goes home justified.
Jesus said: when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and pray to thy Father which is in secret.
Aesop's waggoner, stuck in the mud, called on Hercules and was told to put his shoulder to the wheel.
Nehemiah's builders did both: we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch day and night.
George Herbert says that who sweeps a room as for God's laws makes that and the action fine.
A psalm addresses God by this alone: O thou that hearest prayer, unto thee shall all flesh come.
In the Qur'an God says: I am nigh; I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto me.
Acts says that when the believers had prayed, the place where they were assembled was shaken.
A psalm summons the people to sing unto the Lord and make a joyful noise.
Paul says the Spirit helps our infirmities and makes intercession with groanings which cannot be uttered.
The opening chapter of the Qur'an, said in every prayer, asks only: show us the straight path.
The prayer Jesus taught begins from God's name and kingdom before it asks for daily bread.
A psalm has God say: call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
Bacon noticed that people mark the predictions that hit and never those that miss. How would one honestly test a promise that sincere prayer dispels grief?
James says that the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up.
James recalls Elijah, a man of like passions as we are, who prayed and the heaven gave rain.
Jesus said that where two or three are gathered together in his name, there is he in the midst of them.
Jesus promised that if two shall agree on earth as touching any thing they ask, it shall be done for them.
Paul tells his friends he thanks God upon every remembrance of them, in every prayer making request with joy.
James says: pray one for another; the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
Jesus said that your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him. Why, then, ask?
Paine wrote that a man who prays for rain in sunshine and sunshine in rain is trying to make the Almighty change his mind. What do the readings say prayer changes?
A psalmist says: in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
A centurion asked Jesus to heal at a distance: speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
Exodus says that after Moses pleaded, the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.
Jeremiah hears: call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things.
Jesus compared the kingdom to a grain of mustard seed, the least of seeds, which becomes a tree.
Paul asks that supplications, prayers and intercessions be made on behalf of all.
A psalmist says: I waited patiently for the Lord, and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
Hebrews invites: let us come boldly unto the throne of grace, to find help in time of need.
A psalm asks: let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense, the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.
This is Jacob in the Qur'an: when the bearer of glad tidings laid the shirt on his face, he became a seer once more.
Isaiah has God say: mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
The words are almost the Qur'an's: verily in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest.
Malachi foresees that in every place incense and a pure offering shall be offered to God's name.
Jonah prayed out of the fish's belly: I cried by reason of mine affliction, and he heard me.
A psalm calls God our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
A psalm begins from the lowest place: out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord.
Jesus, on the cross, prayed for those who put him there: Father, forgive them.
Paul tells the Colossians: continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving.
Mark says Jesus rose a great while before day, went out to a solitary place, and there prayed.
Jesus told a parable to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint.
A psalmist admits the condition: if I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.
The priestly blessing asks that the Lord bless thee, and keep thee, and give thee peace.
Daniel says that while he was yet speaking in prayer, the messenger came to him.
Isaiah has God promise: before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
A psalm cries: my God, I cry in the day time, but thou hearest not. What do the readings say to the prayer that meets silence?
A psalm invites: O taste and see that the Lord is good.
Job says: though he slay me, yet will I trust in him.
Daniel prays: we do not present our supplications for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies.
Jesus prays for those who will come after: that they all may be one.
A psalm of thanks begins: bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
Paul's rule was to rejoice evermore, pray without ceasing, and in every thing give thanks.
A psalm says: as the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
Isaiah says that they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength and mount up with wings as eagles.
A psalm says: my soul thirsteth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is.
Emerson called prayer that craves a particular commodity vicious, and true prayer the soliloquy of a beholding and jubilant soul. Is asking for oneself a lower prayer?
A psalm promises refuge under the shadow of the Almighty, and deliverance from the noisome pestilence.
Paul, asking to be rid of an affliction, was answered: my grace is sufficient for thee, for my strength is made perfect in weakness. What of the ailments that prayer does not remove?
The boy Samuel was taught what to say when he was called: speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth.
A psalm ends: let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in thy sight.
A psalm prays: O send out thy light and thy truth; let them lead me.
The Qur'an says: your Lord hath said, pray unto me and I will hear your prayer.
The shepherd of the parable goes after the one that is lost until he find it, and carries it home rejoicing.
David prays before the people: thine, O Lord, is the greatness and the power; all that is in heaven and earth is thine.
A psalmist says: seven times a day do I praise thee, because of thy righteous judgments.
A psalm promises: delight thyself in the Lord, and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
Paul says that eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, what God hath prepared for them that love him.
The first letter of John adds the condition: if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us.
Jesus prayed that the cup might pass from him, and added: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. If God does what he wills, what is the asking for?
A psalmist says to God: put thou my tears into thy bottle; are they not in thy book?
Elijah heard the Lord not in wind, earthquake or fire, but in a still small voice.
Ezekiel sees breath come into the dry bones, and they live and stand upon their feet.
Marcus Aurelius advised turning prayers round: not 'how shall I be released from this?' but 'how shall I not desire to be released?' Which prayer do the readings teach?
Jeremiah asks: is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there?
Joel has God promise: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.
Isaiah calls: ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters.
A psalm promises: the Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in.
Jesus told Peter: I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
While Moses held up his hands Israel prevailed, and when they grew heavy two others held them up.
Jesus spoke of other sheep, not of this fold, and of one fold and one shepherd.
John Wesley recorded in his journal the evening on which he felt his heart strangely warmed.
Zechariah hears: not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.
A sacred tradition has God say: if he comes to me walking, I go to him running.
Job reports those who ask: what is the Almighty, that we should serve him, and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him? What would the readings count as the profit of prayer?
Elisha told his frightened servant: they that be with us are more than they that be with them.
The merchant in the parable sold all that he had for one pearl of great price.
A psalm says: commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him, and he shall bring it to pass.
Tennyson says: speak to him, for he hears; closer is he than breathing, and nearer than hands and feet.
Luke says that Jesus went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
Coleridge's mariner learned that he prayeth best who loveth best all things both great and small.
Tagore tells the worshipper to leave his chanting: God is there where the tiller is tilling the hard ground.
Paul writes of one who might have ministered to him in a friend's stead.
The Qur'an says that the good deeds which endure are better in thy Lord's sight for reward.
Saadi says that every breath taken in prolongs life and every breath given out gladdens the nature, so each breath owes two thanks.
James says that every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights.
Confucius, very sick, was asked for leave to pray for him, and answered: my praying has been for a long time. Can a whole life be the prayer?

psalm-thou-that-hearest-prayer.text: O thou that hearest prayer, unto thee shall all flesh come

psalm-seven-times-a-day.text: Seven times a day do I praise thee because of thy righteous judgments

james-elias-prayed.text: Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months. And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit

mark-what-things-soever-ye-desire.text: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them

colossians-continue-in-prayer.text: Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving

psalm-call-upon-me-in-the-day-of-trouble.text: And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me

psalm-this-poor-man-cried.text: I sought the Lord, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears. They looked unto him, and were lightened: and their faces were not ashamed. This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles

matthew-your-father-knoweth.text: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him

job-what-profit-if-we-pray.text: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him

psalm-if-i-regard-iniquity.text: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me: But verily God hath heard me; he hath attended to the voice of my prayer

ephesians-praying-always.text: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints

exodus-the-lord-repented.text: And the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people

jonah-out-of-the-belly-of-hell.text: Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish's belly, And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice

daniel-whiles-i-was-speaking.text: And whiles I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the Lord my God for the holy mountain of my God; Yea, whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation
